notes:
Company snapshot: mid-market SaaS provider of conversational workflows for customer success teams. Evaluating Redwood as primary inference provider for agent product (multi-tool agents, external API calls, structured responses).

Why Redwood: engineering-led team, cares about measurable latency/cost tradeoffs. Wants consistent API across hosted -> dedicated. Interested in Optimize for batching/quantization recs and Canary + A/B rollouts for agent model changes.

Requirements summary (from product + infra):
- Workload: real-time chat agents with tool calling (calendar, search, backend microservices). ~1200 concurrent active agents peak, average 200-350 qps.
- Latency targets: streaming 95th percentile under 150ms for token latency (customer-facing), end-to-end response latency < 700ms for simple queries. Must support streaming and function-calling hooks.
- Throughput/cost: cost sensitive — wants per-token cost projection. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions to reduce spend.
- Quality guardrails: prompt & eval regression gating on rollout; need A/B + canary rollouts tied to evaluation sets and automatic rollback on regressions.
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logging retention 1 year, EU data residency for EU customers.

Sales/technical timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-12: Initial inbound (marketing playbook) -> AE assigned (Ethan).
- 2025-11-19: Discovery call. Product team: VP Product (Sara Kim), Eng Lead (Carlos Vega). Key ask: streaming + tool calling demo.
- 2025-12-02: Demo (hosted) focused on tool calling flow. Notes: "streaming felt good but want concrete 95p numbers".
- 2025-12-15: Technical deep-dive with SE (Priya) — discussed batching, KV cache, and per-route routing. Priya suggested prefix caching for FAQ flows.
- 2026-01-08: Security review request submitted (SEC-1187). Legal: needs KMS, SOC2 report, data residency statement.
- 2026-01-21: POC kickoff (hosted) — 2-week plan: synthetic traffic + production shadowing of one customer segment. Linked ff call: ff-2026-01-21-helix-poc-call.
- 2026-02-03: Mid-POC checkpoint — streaming spike tests showed 95p at ~220ms on hosted (with default batching). Eng asks for tuning recommendations and cost projections.
- 2026-02-10: Follow-up streaming optimization demo (ff-2026-02-10-streaming-demo). Discussed dedicated sizing and autoscale bursts.
- 2026-02-12: Internal Stakeholders: CFO wants ARR ops model before procurement. Forecast discussion scheduled.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Hosted can meet streaming 95p <= 150-180ms after optimizations OR dedicated sizing estimate that meets target at projected ARR.
- No critical security blockers (KMS + audit logs acceptable).
- Prompt/eval gating: automated regression detection on 10 core prompts (no more than 1% negative drift).

Quoted lines from calls: "If we can't hit 95p for streaming, dedicated is on the table — but show us the delta in cost per 1M tokens." 
"We need canary rollouts for agents; a failed prompt regression at scale is product risk."

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- Engineering wants to start with Hosted to validate functional correctness (tool calling + streaming) before committing to Dedicated. Good candidate for Redwood Optimize to reduce cost while maintaining latency.
- Recommend an A/B plan: 10% traffic canary with eval gating, auto rollback rule on model/eval metric drop. Redwood Console trace hooks requested.
- Action items: SE to deliver tuned batching config + cost modeling by 2026-02-20. AE to present pricing tiers (hosted vs dedicated) and committed capacity estimates.

Decision criteria for move to Dedicated: sustained traffic above 400 qps and hosted 95p still >180ms after tuning OR price per token on hosted exceeds committed Dedicated cost baseline.

Short next steps (choppy CRM style):
- SE deliver perf tuning + cost sheet (due 2026-02-20).
- Host pricing review call w/ CFO (schedule).
- Legal to review KMS + residency doc (SEC-1187).
- Prepare dedicated sizing draft if POC latency can't meet SLOs.
